title: Filtered projective comparison
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring. Consider cochain complexes of $A$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with a globally finite decreasing filtration by subcomplexes [def-sp-filtration]: there are integers $a<b$, independent of cochain degree, with $F^aK=K$ and $F^bK=0$. Morphisms are filtration-preserving chain maps, and homotopies are degree $-1$ maps preserving every filtration step, with $f-g=d_Lh+hd_K$; write $KF(A)$ for the resulting homotopy category, which is the category $\mathcal H_f(A)$ of [def-kun-finite-filtered-module-homotopy]. A filtered quasi-isomorphism is a map inducing a quasi-isomorphism on each associated graded complex [def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients]. Write $DF^-(A)$ and $DF(A)$ for the localizations of the bounded-above and unrestricted homotopy categories at these maps. The localization defining $DF^-(A)$ is equivalent to the homotopy category of bounded-above filtered complexes whose graded modules are projective [def-weil-pbc-projective-module] in every degree. Every bounded-above filtered complex $K$ admits a filtered quasi-isomorphism $Q\to K$ from such a filtered projective complex. Moreover, if $Q$ is bounded above with projective graded modules, and $E$ is any filtered complex, without a bound on its cochain degrees, then the canonical map $\operatorname{Hom}_{KF(A)}(Q,E)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{DF(A)}(Q,E)$ is bijective; the group on the left consists of filtration-preserving chain maps modulo filtration-preserving homotopy. All these assertions also hold when every complex, map and homotopy is restricted throughout to two-step filtrations $0\subset K'\subset K$, embedded as $F^pK=K$ for $p\leq0$, $F^1K=K'$ and $F^pK=0$ for $p\geq2$, and only the two graded complexes $K'$ and $K/K'$ are tested for quasi-isomorphisms; in particular a two-step $K$ has a two-step replacement $Q'\subset Q$. For a two-step bounded-above projective source and an arbitrary two-step target, inclusion into the globally finite filtered localization induces a bijection on morphisms: both localizations have the same chain-map-modulo-filtered-homotopy description just stated.

source.place: Tag 03TB (trace-lemma-filtered-derived-category), bounded-above projective comparison; Tag 03TJ (trace-section-filtrations-perfect), fully faithful bounded finite-projective models in unbounded DF. The unrestricted-target bounded-above assertion and the comparison with two-step filtrations are the filtered K-projective extension of this comparison, not assertions printed verbatim in Tag 03TB; their argument is described in the worker report.

proof.text: First establish the module-level lifting used below. Call a filtered surjection $v:B\to C$ strict if $v(F^pB)=F^pC$ for every $p$. A finite filtered module $P$ with projective graded modules splits as a filtered module: choose sections of each surjection $F^pP\to\operatorname{gr}^pP$, using the lifting characterization of projectivity, and proceed downwards through the finite filtration. Thus $P\cong\bigoplus_{a\le p<b}P_p$, with $P_p\cong\operatorname{gr}^pP$ and $F^rP=\bigoplus_{p\ge r}P_p$. A filtered map $P\to C$ lifts along a strict filtered surjection $B\to C$: lift its restriction on each projective $P_p$ along the surjection $F^pB\to F^pC$, then add these finitely many lifts. Also every filtered module $M$ with bounds $a,b$ admits a strict filtered surjection from a filtered free module. Take the free module $U(M)$ on the set of pairs $(p,x)$ with $a\le p<b$ and $x\in F^pM$, let $F^rU(M)$ be spanned by pairs with $p\ge r$, and send the basis vector $(p,x)$ to $x$. For $a\le r<b$ the vectors $(r,x)$ lift all $x\in F^rM$; the cases $r<a$ and $r\ge b$ are immediate. Its $p$-th graded module is free on the pairs of weight exactly $p$, hence projective. These statements use arbitrary free modules, with no finite-generation assumption.

source.place: Tag 03TB (lemma-filtered-derived-category), omitted projective proof: filtered splitting and enough filtered projectives; Algebra Tags 05CE (definition-projective), 05CF (lemma-characterize-projective).

proof.text:
Now construct the replacement, rather than applying the omitted assertion of Tag 03TB. Fix $K^j=0$ for $j>c$ and global filtration bounds $a,b$. Put $Q^j=0$ above $c$ and construct $q:Q\to K$ downwards. At stage $n\le c$, suppose all terms and maps in degrees $j>n$ have been constructed, $q^j$ is a strict filtered surjection there, and, writing $N^j=\ker q^j$ with the induced filtration, every complex $F^pN$ is exact in degrees $j>n+1$. Define the filtered module
$$B^n=\{(k,x)\in K^n\oplus Q^{n+1}:d_Kk=q^{n+1}x,\ d_Qx=0\},\qquad F^pB^n=B^n\cap(F^pK^n\oplus F^pQ^{n+1}).$$
The projection $B^n\to K^n$ is strict and surjective. Indeed, for $k\in F^pK^n$, choose $x_0\in F^pQ^{n+1}$ lifting $d_Kk$. Then $d_Qx_0\in F^pN^{n+2}$ is a cycle; the induction hypothesis gives $y\in F^pN^{n+1}$ with $d_Qy=d_Qx_0$. Put $x=x_0-y$. Choose the strict filtered free cover $Q^n=U(B^n)\to B^n$ from step 1 and define $q^n,d_Q^n$ by its two projections. The equations defining $B^n$ give $q^{n+1}d_Q^n=d_Kq^n$ and $d_Q^{n+1}d_Q^n=0$, and $q^n$ is strict surjective. For a cycle $x\in F^pN^{n+1}$, the pair $(0,x)\in F^pB^n$ lifts to $z\in F^pQ^n$ with $q^nz=0$ and $d_Qz=x$. Thus $F^pN$ is now exact in degree $n+1$, establishing the next induction hypothesis. Above $c$ all objects are zero, so the initial hypotheses hold. Induction on $c-n$ constructs all degrees, with the same $a,b$ in every degree; no limiting operation on modules is involved.

source.place: Tag 03TB (lemma-filtered-derived-category), omitted projective proof: explicit downward filtered free resolution.

proof.text: The construction gives a filtered quasi-isomorphism $q:Q\to K$. For each integer $p$, $F^pN$ is acyclic, because its exactness in any fixed degree is established at a finite stage of step 2. Consequently $\operatorname{gr}^pN$ is acyclic as well: represent a graded cycle by $z\in F^pN^n$, so $dz\in F^{p+1}N^{n+1}$; exactness there gives $w\in F^{p+1}N^n$ with $dw=dz$. Then $z-w$ is a cycle in $F^pN$, hence $z-w=dv$ for some $v\in F^pN^{n-1}$. Thus the original graded cycle is a boundary. Strict surjectivity of $q$ gives a degreewise exact sequence $0\to\operatorname{gr}^pN\to\operatorname{gr}^pQ\to\operatorname{gr}^pK\to0$. For the kernel assertion, if $x\in F^pQ$ has $qx\in F^{p+1}K$, lift $qx$ to $y\in F^{p+1}Q$ and replace $x$ by $x-y\in F^pN$. Finally a degreewise surjective chain map $t:V\to W$ with acyclic kernel $J$ is a quasi-isomorphism. For $w\in Z^nW$ lift $w$ to $v\in V^n$. Then $dv\in Z^{n+1}J$, so $dv=du$ for $u\in J^n$; $v-u$ is a cycle mapping to $w$. If $v\in Z^nV$ and $tv=dw$ with $w\in W^{n-1}$, lift $w$ to $y\in V^{n-1}$. Now $v-dy\in Z^nJ$, hence $v-dy=dz$ for $z\in J^{n-1}$ and $v=d(y+z)$. These are surjectivity and injectivity on cohomology. Apply this chase to the displayed graded sequence. Each graded module of $Q^n$ is projective by step 1, so $Q$ has every claimed replacement property.

source.place: Tag 03TB (lemma-filtered-derived-category), omitted proof: verification of the constructed replacement on all associated graded complexes.

proof.text: For the comparison with unbounded targets, first let $E$ be any globally finite filtered complex whose graded complexes are acyclic. Every $F^pE$ is acyclic. To see this without assuming that cycles commute with grading, take an actual cycle $z\in F^pE^n$. Acyclicity of $\operatorname{gr}^pE$ gives $y_p\in F^pE^{n-1}$ with $z-dy_p\in F^{p+1}E^n$. This residual element is still a cycle. Repeat at $p+1$, then at $p+2$, until $F^bE=0$; summing the finitely many primitives gives $z=d(\sum y_i)$ inside $F^pE$. For $p<a$ use $F^pE=E=F^aE$, and for $p\ge b$ there is nothing to prove. In particular, if $Z^nE=\ker(d:E^n\to E^{n+1})$ has its induced filtration, $d:E^{n-1}\to Z^nE$ is a strict filtered surjection. This is a finite filtration argument, with no hypothesis on the cochain support of $E$.

source.place: Tag 03TB (lemma-filtered-derived-category), omitted comparison argument extended to unbounded targets: exactness of every filtration step.

proof.text:
Let $Q$ be bounded above with projective graded modules, and let $u:Q\to E$ be a filtered chain map into such a graded-acyclic $E$. Construct a filtered null homotopy $h^n:Q^n\to E^{n-1}$ downwards from the top cochain degree of $Q$. Set $h^n=0$ above that degree. Suppose the homotopy equations hold in all degrees above $n$ and put $r^n=u^n-h^{n+1}d_Q^n$. This has image in $Z^nE$, since
$$d_Er^n=u^{n+1}d_Q^n-d_Eh^{n+1}d_Q^n=h^{n+2}d_Q^{n+1}d_Q^n=0.$$
It preserves every filtration step. By the module-level lifting of step 1 and the strict surjection $d:E^{n-1}\to Z^nE$ of step 4, choose a filtered lift $h^n$ of $r^n$. Then $u^n=d_Eh^n+h^{n+1}d_Q^n$. This proves the induction and constructs a null homotopy in every degree. Each degree is reached after finitely many steps, although $Q$ need not be bounded below. The same conclusion applies to any cochain shift of a graded-acyclic $E$, using the unchanged filtration indices and the usual signed shift differential.

source.place: Tag 03TB (lemma-filtered-derived-category), omitted proof: explicit filtered K-projective null homotopy; Tag 03TJ (section-filtrations-perfect), unbounded comparison specialization.

proof.text: Let $s:X\to Y$ be a filtered quasi-isomorphism, with $X,Y$ arbitrary, and fix a bounded-above filtered projective $Q$. If $X,Y$ have filtration bounds $a_X,b_X$ and $a_Y,b_Y$, their direct sum has bounds $\min(a_X,a_Y),\max(b_X,b_Y)$. Give $C=\operatorname{Cone}(s)$ the direct-sum filtration, so $C^n=Y^n\oplus X^{n+1}$ and $d_C(y,x)=(d_Yy+s x,-d_Xx)$. The graded quotient of this direct sum is the direct sum of the graded quotients, with the same displayed differential, hence $\operatorname{gr}^pC=\operatorname{Cone}(\operatorname{gr}^ps)$. The ordinary cone criterion makes each graded complex acyclic, so step 5 applies to $C$ and $C[-1]$. For surjectivity of $s_*:\operatorname{Hom}_{KF}(Q,X)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{KF}(Q,Y)$, take $f:Q\to Y$ and null-homotope $(f,0):Q\to C$. Write this homotopy as $(a,b)$, where $a^n:Q^n\to Y^{n-1}$ and $b^n:Q^n\to X^n$. Its equations say $d_Xb=bd_Q$ and $f-sb=d_Ya+ad_Q$. Thus $b$ is a filtered chain map with $s_*[b]=[f]$. For injectivity suppose $g:Q\to X$ and $sg=d_Ya+ad_Q$. In $C[-1]^n=Y^{n-1}\oplus X^n$ the differential is $(y,x)\mapsto(-d_Yy-sx,d_Xx)$, and $(-a,g):Q\to C[-1]$ is a filtered chain map. A null homotopy of it has second component $e^n:Q^n\to X^{n-1}$ satisfying $g=d_Xe+ed_Q$. Thus $[g]=0$. Applying this to the difference of two maps proves injectivity. Consequently $\operatorname{Hom}_{KF}(Q,-)$ inverts every filtered quasi-isomorphism, including ones between unbounded complexes.

source.place: Tags 014E (derived-definition-cone), 05RT (derived-lemma-acyclic), and 03TB (trace-lemma-filtered-derived-category): explicit cone proof of inversion by Hom from a filtered projective source.

proof.text:
Here is the categorical passage to the localization, with no boundedness assumption hidden in a fraction theorem. Put $\mathcal C=KF(A)$, $L:\mathcal C\to DF(A)$, and $H=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(Q,-)$, a functor to sets in a common sufficiently large universe. Step 6 says that $H$ inverts all denominators. By the localization universal property (1) there are $\overline H:DF(A)\to\mathbf{Set}$ and $\phi:\overline H L\cong H$. Put $B=\operatorname{Hom}_{DF(A)}(LQ,-)$; its restriction also inverts denominators. The natural map $\tau:H\to BL$, $f\mapsto Lf$, lifts by part (2) of the same cited statement to $\eta:\overline H\to B$, with $\eta_{LE}=\tau_E\phi_E$. Define
$$e=\phi_Q^{-1}(1_Q),\qquad r_E(\alpha)=\phi_E\bigl(\overline H(\alpha)(e)\bigr)\quad(\alpha:LQ\to LE).$$
Naturality of $\phi$ gives $r_E(Lf)=f$. Naturality of $\eta$ gives
$$L(r_E(\alpha))=\eta_{LE}(\overline H(\alpha)e)=B(\alpha)(\eta_{LQ}(e))=\alpha,$$
since $\eta_{LQ}(e)=L(1_Q)=1_{LQ}$. Thus $r_E$ and $f\mapsto Lf$ are inverse bijections, exactly the claimed comparison with unrestricted targets. The identical argument applies to the localization of the bounded-above subcategory, because step 6 applies in particular to all its denominators. This argument uses only functor and natural-transformation factorization, not the abelian-category theorem about ordinary K-projective complexes.

source.place: Categories Tag 04VG (lemma-properties-left-localization), part (3), together with the natural-transformation lifting in the cited Mathlib universal-property node; application to Tag 03TB.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal P^-$ be the full subcategory of $KF^-(A)$ on the bounded-above filtered complexes with projective graded modules. Step 7, applied in the bounded-above homotopy category, says its composite functor to $DF^-(A)$ is fully faithful. Steps 2 and 3 show every object of $DF^-(A)$ is isomorphic to the image of an object of $\mathcal P^-$ via a filtered quasi-isomorphism. Explicitly, choose for every bounded-above $K$ one replacement $q_K:Q_K\to K$. For a localized morphism $\alpha:K\to K'$, define its inverse-equivalence image to be the unique homotopy class $Q_K\to Q_{K'}$ whose localized image is $L(q_{K'})^{-1}\alpha L(q_K)$, using the bijection in step 7. Uniqueness verifies identities and composition; the $L(q_K)$ give the counit isomorphisms. For a projective object the same bijection lifts these isomorphisms and their inverses, giving the unit. This exhibits the asserted equivalence and specifies that it is induced by the localization functor.

source.place: Tag 03TB (lemma-filtered-derived-category), projective equivalence, now deduced from the explicit replacement and comparison.

proof.text: Finally run the entire argument in the category of two-step filtrations with the fixed bounds $a=0,b=2$. The free cover of step 1 has weights only $0,1$, so the construction in step 2 stays in two-step filtrations and produces $Q'\subset Q$ with projective graded modules $Q'$ and $Q/Q'$. Kernels, cycles, direct sums, cones and cochain shifts used in steps 3--6 retain these same two filtration indices. Thus testing the two graded complexes is precisely the test used in every argument, and step 7 applies to the separate two-step localization as well. A map or homotopy between two such embedded complexes preserves all filtration indices exactly when it preserves the one specified subcomplex. Hence its homotopy-category Hom set agrees with the corresponding Hom set in $KF(A)$. For a bounded-above two-step projective $Q$ and an arbitrary two-step $E$, the canonical Hom bijections of step 7 for the two localizations both send a chain-map class $[f]$ to its localization. Inclusion preserves denominators, hence induces the functor between the two localizations; its Hom map intertwines those two bijections and is therefore bijective. This proves every two-step assertion, including unbounded targets, without replacing filtration-preserving maps by strict maps.
